chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Captives from Yemen were brought to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). When they reached Al-Juhfa, their expenses ran out, so they sold a girl from the captives, whose mother was with them. When they arrived at the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), he heard her crying and said: "What is this crying?" They said: "O Messenger Allah, we needed expenses, so we sold her daughter." He sent for her price, and she was brought back, and he said: "Sell them both together or keep both of them together."'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on separating a mother and daughter when selling slaves?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the Prophet’s (PBUH) sensitivity to familial bonds even within the context of war captives, establishing a key juristic principle regarding the separation of mahram relatives. It underscores the Shia legal emphasis on preserving family integrity during the transaction of slaves, influencing discussions on 'firq' (separation) in fiqh. The incident at Al-Juhfa serves as a practical precedent for ensuring that economic necessity does not override kinship ties.
